inputs.original_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a prolife law, arguing that limiting abortion violates freedom of religion. The claim, brought by the American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice, argued that an Indiana law “violates religious freedoms by burdening the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with their sincerely held beliefs.” Judge Christina R. [...] The post This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right appeared first on LifeNews.com .
inputs.modified_text: An Indiana judge blocked a law that restricted abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened religious freedom. The claim that this “turns liberty on its head” ignores who bears the cost when the state dictates what people may do with their bodies. Religious freedom cannot mean privileging one moral view while denying others the ability to make deeply personal decisions. Calling abortion a threat to society’s moral foundations only obscures the power imbalance: lawmakers should not impose their beliefs at the expense of people who need reproductive care.
